pattern.description: From a full-window view of the Cursor 3 agent reply, the frame pushes in about 2x toward the lower-left, ending on the summary list, the sidebar and the Review / Commit & Push buttons, where the pointer hovers on Review as the voice-over says 'You can look at changes'.
pattern.why_premium: A fast, eased push-in turns a dense full-screen UI into a legible close-up and lands on the exact control the narration names (Review). The viewer never has to search the screen.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.fromTo(uiWrapper,{scale:1,xPercent:0,yPercent:0},{scale:2,xPercent:17,yPercent:-16,transformOrigin:'30% 85%',duration:0.45,ease:'power2.inOut'}); then tween the pointer to the Review button: gsap.to(pointer,{x:reviewX,y:reviewY,duration:0.4,ease:'power2.out'},'-=0.1')
build_hint.remotion: const p = spring({frame, fps, config:{damping:200, stiffness:100, mass:1}}) (no overshoot, critically damped feel). scale = interpolate(p,[0,1],[1,2]). Translate the wrapper toward the lower-left with interpolate on the same p. Pointer position interpolates to the Review button with Easing.out(Easing.cubic).

notes: Camera verdict is push_in (scale about 1.99), so the UI scale-up is a camera/zoom move on a screen recording rather than element animation. The energy curve shows a near-instant start at f742 and a stop at f754, which suggests an ease_in_out or even a near-linear zoom, so measure it. The pointer's motion is uncertain (it may only ride the zoom). All four SFX candidates are unsure; the reverse-swoosh CLAP labels are probably speech or music residue.
